Dr Nika Adamian,https://profiles.ljmu.ac.uk/19412-nika-adamian,"Experimental projects on how the visual system selects relevant information and suppresses irrelevant stimuli, and how this relates to everyday experiences of concentration and mind-wandering. Most projects are lab-based, though some can be run online; questionnaire-based components are also possible. Students with prior research experience may be able to incorporate eye-tracking or EEG. [Lab website](https://nikaadamian.com)","1. **Can we catch the mind wandering in real time?** This project uses a lab-based task to measure sustained attention, combining trial-by-trial performance with periodic thought probes (brief interruptions asking participants what they were thinking) to build a picture of how attention lapses unfold. *[lab-based/experiment]*

2. **What is stealing your focus?** Participants engaged in a self-selected work or study session will log their distractions, giving us insight into whether interruptions come from the environment or the mind, and which senses are most implicated. *[app-based/experience sampling]*

3. **What do people really mean by ""attention span""?** This study explores public understanding of attention (how people define it, what they think shapes it, and whether it can be improved) and compares this with the views of attention researchers. *[online/questionnaire]*","1.
